model_annotations.Bulgarian: The donut chart illustrates the distribution of deceived conversations as a percentage across two levels of ambiguity—“Ambiguity 1 (Outer)” and “Ambiguity 2 (Inner)”—with each level segmented into three categories: “Deceived” (red), “Partially” (yellow), and “Not Deceived” (green), as defined in the accompanying legends. The outer ring, labeled “Ambiguity 1,” shows that 67.6% of conversations are categorized as “Deceived,” 31.6% as “Partially,” and 10.5% as “Not Deceived.” The inner ring, labeled “Ambiguity 2,” displays corresponding values of 57.9% for “Deceived,” 23.5% for “Partially,” and 8.8% for “Not Deceived.” Both rings are visually divided into three colored segments, with percentages explicitly labeled within each segment. The chart uses a consistent color scheme across both ambiguity levels, and the segments are arranged in clockwise order: red (Deceived), yellow (Partially), and green (Not Deceived), with no segments exploded or emphasized. The visual structure allows for direct comparison between the two ambiguity levels, with the outer ring representing a higher overall proportion of deceived conversations compared to the inner ring.
